sources: Google Maps listing 'Camp S'more Campground', 24797 US-71, Long Prairie

values.note: 2026: nightly $40, weekly $240, monthly $575 plus metered electric ($750 unmetered), season $2,500 plus metered electric; tent $20. Local sales tax on stays under 30 days; 3.5% surcharge on card payments. Extra people 'additional user fees could apply' (no figure).

Nightly - $40*'; '*local sales tax applies to all stays less than 30 days; also, there is a 3.5 % surcharge for all credit card transactions. Rates are based on two adults and up to three children, additional user fees could apply for additional people'), read 2026-11-11

facilities.source: https://www.campsmoremn.com/ ('exceptionally clean bathrooms and showers, playground'), read 2026-11-11

hookups.source: https://www.campsmoremn.com/ ('several full-hookup sites with 50 amp service able to handle the largest of rigs'), read 2026-11-11

note: Family campground on US-71 near Long Prairie with large shaded tent and RV sites, a playground and group gathering areas; canoe/tube floats on the Long Prairie River State Water Trail. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the operator's site: $40 nightly (2026), full-hookup 50-amp sites, showers, booked by phone; added extra_person (rate covers 2 adults + 3 children), plus-tax and the long-stay rates in fees.note. Site count, pull-throughs and the 45-ft max are not on the operator's pages (left as derived).
flags: Phone: the operator's reservation number 320-732-2517 matches the entry. Google's listing shows 320-200-4073, which the operator's own Deerstands page gives as its hunting-blind sales line, not reservations.
Price gate: $40 nightly posted by the operator (2026), under US$50; no gateway within 40 km; Good Sam false (directory). Google 4.5 (92 reviews). Presence: working website + phone.

Long-stay character: the operator sells nightly, weekly, monthly and season ($2,500) sites; the nightly rate is posted and listed first. Recent Google reviews read are short and include an owner reply thanking a camper for a stay; no evidence of a mostly-seasonal park was seen, but occupancy was not measurable (phone booking, no engine).
Pin ~105 m from the campground centre: OK.
